title: The Epstein Files Collection — archive index of official releases, mirrors, torrents and checksums
description:
Where to read the Epstein files, where to download them, and how to check that what you got is genuine.

A catalogue of the public record released under the Epstein Files Transparency Act (H.R.4405) and related DOJ, House Oversight and court productions. It holds no documents — a few hundred kilobytes of metadata describing terabytes of material on justice.gov, the Internet Archive and in BitTorrent swarms.

Contents

  • official_library.json — snapshot of the DOJ Epstein Library — 76 entries: the 12 EFTA Data Sets, 51 individually named court records, FOIA productions and prior disclosures
  • datasets.json — 12 releases with every official URL, mirror and magnet, and 34 published SHA-256 checksums
  • torrents.json — 57 distinct torrents keyed by infohash
  • derivatives.json — 24 third-party processed corpora — OCR text, email sets, embeddings
  • viewers.json — 11 browser-based readers and search interfaces
  • health.json — weekly probe of 243 pointers recording which still resolve, and when each last worked

Plus flat magnet and link lists, a generated manifest, and plain-language guides for readers who are not programmers. Field-level schemas are documented in docs/DATA_DICTIONARY.md.

Tools (Python, standard library only): aggregate.py rebuilds the index from a curated source list; verify.py identifies a file you already downloaded against the recorded checksums; healthcheck.py detects link rot; render_docs.py generates the guides.

Limits worth knowing

  • Checksums are transcribed from whoever published each mirror, not independently re-verified here.
  • Data Set 9 is incomplete at the source — files were removed after publication, and volunteer reconstructions cover more of it than the official ZIP.
  • Derivative corpora are other people's pipelines, unvetted for OCR quality, coverage or redaction handling.
  • In link health, blocked (401/403/429) is not gone: bot protection is indistinguishable from withdrawal at probe level.

Only publicly released material is indexed. These records concern the sexual abuse of children and contain victim information; being named in an investigative file is not evidence of wrongdoing.
